title: Graphing a Continuous Triangular Piecewise Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of the piecewise-defined function f(x) = x for 0 <= x <= 1, and f(x) = 2 - x for 1 < x <= 2.
finalAnswer: \text{Triangular peak on } [0, 2] \text{ rising from } (0, 0) \text{ to } (1, 1) \text{ and falling to } (2, 0)

steps.title: Graph the First Linear Branch on [0, 1]
steps.explanation: On the closed interval [0, 1], f(x) = x is the line segment of slope 1 connecting the origin (0, 0) to the point (1, 1).
steps.why: A linear rule on a closed interval graphs as the straight line segment joining its endpoint values.

steps.title: Graph the Second Linear Branch on (1, 2]
steps.explanation: On (1, 2], f(x) = 2 - x is a line segment of slope -1. As x -> 1^+, 2 - x -> 1, so the second segment connects seamlessly to the point (1, 1) and descends to (2, 0).
steps.why: Because the left-hand value f(1) = 1 matches the right-hand limit 2 - 1 = 1, the two segments meet without a jump at (1, 1).

steps.title: Summarize the Complete Graph, Domain, and Range
steps.explanation: The complete graph is a continuous tent-shaped (triangular) curve on [0, 2] with apex at (1, 1) and base endpoints at (0, 0) and (2, 0).
steps.why: Combining the two contiguous intervals [0, 1] and (1, 2] yields the domain [0, 2] and output range [0, 1].
